assertion.name: LMNB1 ADLD-1-TO upstream deletion (approximately 660 kb)
assertion.description: Heterozygous deletion reported by Giorgio et al. in the ADLD-1-TO family, spanning hg19 chr5:125385805-126043053 and ending approximately 66 kb upstream of the LMNB1 promoter. The interval removes GRAMD3, ALDH7A1, and PHAX and intervening sequence while sparing LMNB1 itself. Its ADLD mechanism is altered regulation of LMNB1 rather than deletion of LMNB1 coding sequence. Lamin B1 excess was demonstrated in frontal-lobe postmortem tissue. The original study proposed forebrain enhancer adoption; later work implicates loss of an oligodendrocyte silencer and leaves the additional requirement for ectopic enhancers unresolved.

assertion.description: The single recurrent ADSA allele. A rare non-synonymous substitution at a well-conserved residue, predicted deleterious by multiple in silico tools. assertion.name: In-frame exon-skipping genomic deletions (exons 3-5, exons 14-16)
assertion.description: A distinct allele class alongside the predominant truncating (nonsense/frameshift/splice) alleles. Genomic deletions remove exons 3-5 or exons 14-16 from the transcript without shifting the reading frame, so the resulting ADAMTS2 protein is missing an internal domain rather than being absent or grossly truncated. Neither deleted region had previously been recognised as functionally critical, but aminoprocollagen processing was still strongly impaired, so this class extends the requirement for intact enzyme structure beyond the domains already implicated by nonsense alleles.

functional_effects.description: Removing exons 3-5 or exons 14-16 leaves the reading frame intact, so the protein is internally shortened rather than truncated or absent, yet aminoprocollagen processing is still strongly impaired both in vitro and in vivo. The affected domains had not previously been recognised as crucial for ADAMTS-2 activity.

selected_evidence.snippet: The first patient was homozygous for a genomic deletion causing an in-frame skipping of exons 3-5 in the transcript. In the second patient, the allele inherited from the mother lacks exon 3, generating a premature stop codon, whereas the paternal allele has a genomic deletion resulting in an in-frame skipping of exons 14-16 at the mRNA level.
